heroSummary: The enclosed Bambu Lab P1S handles Polymaker PolyLite ASA right out of the box, reaching safe print speeds up to 202 mm/s based on its 17 mm³/s volumetric flow limit. Thanks to the fully enclosed chamber and standard stainless steel nozzle compatibility, thermal stability is easily maintained without hardware modifications.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with PVP glue stick or liquid adhesive as a release agent
slicerTweaks: Set Max Volumetric Speed to 17 mm³/s in the filament profile to cap continuous high-speed flow within safe melt limits.
Disable the chamber exhaust fan and set Part Cooling Fan to 10% min / 25% max with a 30s layer time threshold to prevent layer delamination.
Adjust Bed Temperature to 98°C for all layers and set First Layer Speed to 35 mm/s to ensure robust build plate adhesion.
Enable a 5mm outer brim with 0.1mm brim-object gap in Others tab to protect high-stress corners from lifting.

troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Excessive chamber draft and thermal shrinkage of ASA when printed below optimal chamber ambient temperature.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Preheat the bed at 100°C for 15 minutes with the chamber closed before printing, use a 5mm brim, and set bed temperature to 98°C.

troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Part cooling fan running too fast or chamber exhaust fan actively cooling the part during printing.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Turn off the chamber fan completely in the filament start G-code/OrcaSlicer fan settings, and cap part cooling between 10% and 25%.

troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Moisture absorption in the hygroscopic ASA filament or insufficient retraction length on the direct drive extruder.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the filament spool at 70°C for 6 to 8 hours and ensure retraction distance is set to 0.8 mm with 30 mm/s retraction speed.

faq.question: Does Polymaker PolyLite ASA require a hardened steel nozzle on the P1S?
faq.answer: No, PolyLite ASA is non-abrasive, so the stock stainless steel nozzle on the Bambu Lab P1S is fully compatible and will not suffer premature wear.

faq.question: Can I reach 202 mm/s print speed across all features?
faq.answer: Yes, standard walls and infill can run at 202 mm/s under a 0.2mm layer height and 0.42mm line width, but slow down outer walls to around 100-120 mm/s and the first layer to 35 mm/s for surface quality and adhesion.

faq.question: Should I print with the P1S door or top lid open?
faq.answer: Keep both the door and top glass lid completely closed during printing to retain heat and prevent rapid cooling that causes warping and cracking in ASA.

faq.question: How should I handle the styrene emissions produced by ASA?
faq.answer: Ensure the P1S carbon filter is properly seated, run the print in a well-ventilated room, or vent the exhaust port externally, as ASA produces VOCs during extrusion.
